title: Quantum Information-Theoretic Analysis of Optical Fiber Sensing via Stimulated Brillouin Scattering
abstract: Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is a powerful mechanism for distributed sensing in optical fibers, as the Brillouin response is highly sensitive to local material parameters. Assuming the input probe is a quantum state, we develop a quantum-information-theoretic framework for SBS-based fiber sensing and intrusion detection. Starting from a linearized opto-acoustic Hamiltonian, we derive an effective input-output relation for a short fiber segment. We then model each fiber segment as a single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel and the entire fiber as a cascade of quantum channels. We then compute the quantum Fisher information for general SBS-dependent parameters and identify optimal measurement settings to achieve the quantum limit, comparing them with receiver-constrained strategies such as heterodyne detection and photon counting. In addition, we propose an adaptive approach that achieves first-order asymptotic optimality and provides a novel second-order correction to address preliminary miscalibration. As an application, we apply the framework to the fiber-tapping detection problem.
summary: This paper establishes a quantum information-theoretic framework to analyze sensing using Stimulated Brillouin Scattering (SBS) in optical fibers. By modeling the fiber as a cascade of bosonic Gaussian channels, the authors calculate the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) to determine the ultimate precision limit. This is crucial for developing next-generation, quantum-enhanced fiber sensing and intrusion detection systems.
main_problem: The paper develops a quantum information-theoretic framework to determine the fundamental quantum limits for sensing using Stimulated Brillouin Scattering (SBS) in optical fibers.
main_result: The framework successfully computes the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) for SBS-dependent parameters, identifying optimal measurement strategies that approach the quantum limit.
method: The analysis models the fiber segment as a bosonic Gaussian quantum channel and employs the Symmetric Logarithmic Derivative (SLD) formalism to calculate the QFI.
model_or_system: The physical system is an optical fiber utilizing SBS, modeled by a linearized opto-acoustic Hamiltonian. The evolution is treated as a cascade of single-mode bosonic Gaussian channels.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), optimal measurement settings, and the output state (displaced thermal state).
important_parameters: Brillouin frequency shift ($\Omega_B/2\pi$), linewidth ($\Gamma_B/2\pi$), and the input pump power ($P_p$).
main_assumptions: The optical pump field is assumed to be strong enough to be approximated by a classical coherent field, and the analysis relies on small-segment approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the Lorentzian SBS gain spectrum; Figure 2 illustrates the interacting probe, pump, and Stokes photons; subsequent figures detail the dependence of power factors and QFI on parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the input-output relation for a small fiber segment (modeling it as a bosonic Gaussian channel) to calculating the QFI using the SLD formalism, culminating in applications to fiber-tapping detection.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantum limit analysis for a practical quantum sensing platform (optical fiber), bridging quantum information theory with applied quantum optics.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Normalized Brillouin gain spectrum for a standard silica single-mode fiber near 1550 nm with parameters summarized in Table I. At zero detuning, the gain is maximum. It then decreases rapidly with a linewidth set by ΓB.

Figure 4. Short-segment SBS power factor |µi(Ω)|2 as a function of detuning ∆f = (Ω−ΩB)/2π using representative parameters for a standard silica single-mode fiber near 1550 nm, summarized in Tables I and II.

Figure 3. Real and imaginary parts of the Brillouin response using representative parameters for a standard silica single-mode fiber near 1550 nm, summarized in Tables I and II. In both panels, the real part gives the resonant SBS gain response, while the imaginary part gives the dispersive phase response and changes sign across the Brillouin resonance.

Figure 5. SBS-induced phonon-noise spectrum |νi(Ω)|2 as a function of detuning ∆f = (Ω−ΩB)/2π using representative parameters for a standard silica single-mode fiber near 1550 nm, summarized in Tables I and II.

Figure 6. Coherent (solid) and thermal (dashed) contributions to the quantum Fisher information per mode for estimating the Brillouin frequency fB, as a function of the input probe photon number E. For Pp = 10 mW and ∆f = 10 MHz, Fcoh increases linearly with E, whereas Fth remains constant. The contributions become equal at E∗≈6.35 × 105 photons per mode, marking the transition from thermal to coherent information dominance.
